arxiv-2007-11884.title: Quantum Secrecy in Thermal States III
arxiv-2007-11884.creator: Anne Ghesquière, Benjamin T. H. Varcoe
arxiv-2007-11884.description: Abstract In this paper we expanded the security of a central broadcast protocol using thermal states to the case in which the eavesdropper controls the source. Quantum secrecy in a continuous variable central broadcast scheme is guaranteed by the quantum correlations present in thermal states arising from the Hanbury Brown and Twiss effect.

arxiv-2202-13290.title: ICASSP 2022 Acoustic Echo Cancellation Challenge
arxiv-2202-13290.creator: Ross Cutler, Ando Saabas, Tanel Parnamaa, Marju Purin, Hannes Gamper, Sebastian Braun, Karsten Sørensen, Robert Aichner
arxiv-2202-13290.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ross Cutler, Ando Saabas, Tanel Parnamaa, Marju Purin, Hannes Gamper, Sebastian Braun, Karsten Sørensen, Robert Aichner. The ICASSP 2022 Acoustic Echo Cancellation Challenge is intended to stimulate research in acoustic echo cancellation (AEC), which is an important area of speech enhancement and still a top issue in audio communication. This is the third AEC challenge and it is enhanced by including mobile scenarios, adding speech recognition word accuracy rate as a metric, and making the audio 48 kHz.

arxiv-2204-07576.title: The Distributed Information Bottleneck reveals the explanatory structure of complex systems
arxiv-2204-07576.creator: Kieran A. Murphy 1, Dani S. Bassett 1,2,3,4,5,6,7
arxiv-2204-07576.description: Abstract The fruits of science are relationships made comprehensible, often by way of approximation. While deep learning is an extremely powerful way to find relationships in data, its use in science has been hindered by the difficulty of understanding the learned relationships. arxiv-2204-09329.title: Deterministic Distributed algorithms and Descriptive Combinatorics on Δ \Delta -regular trees This paper is an extension of some parts of the conference paper “Local Problems on Trees from the Perspectives of Distributed Algorithms, Finitary Factors, and Descriptive Combinatorics (arXiv:2106.02066)”
arxiv-2204-09329.creator: Sebastian Brandt, Yi-Jun Chang, Jan Grebík, Christoph Grunau, Václav Rozhoň, Zoltán Vidnyánszky
arxiv-2204-09329.description: Abstract We study complexity classes of local problems on regular trees from the perspective of distributed local algorithms and descriptive combinatorics. We show that, surprisingly, some deterministic local complexity classes from the hierarchy of distributed computing exactly coincide with well studied classes of problems in descriptive combinatorics.

arxiv-2206-02050.title: Learning Speaker-specific Lip-to-Speech Generation
arxiv-2206-02050.creator: 1 Munender Varshney 3 , 1 Ravindra Yadav 2 , Vinay P. Namboodiri 4 and Rajesh M Hegde 2
arxiv-2206-02050.description: Abstract Understanding the lip movement and inferring the speech from it is notoriously difficult for the common person. The task of accurate lip-reading gets help from various cues of the speaker and its contextual or environmental setting. Every speaker has a different accent and speaking style, which can be inferred from their visual and speech features.

arxiv-2310-19708.title: COMBINING LANGUAGE MODELS FOR SPECIALIZED DOMAINS: A COLORFUL APPROACH
arxiv-2310-19708.creator: D. Eitan, M. Pirchi, N. Glazer, S. Meital, G. Ayach, G. Krendel, A. Shamsian, A. Navon, G. Hetz, J. Keshet
arxiv-2310-19708.description: Abstract General purpose language models (LMs) encounter difficulties when processing domain-specific jargon and terminology, which are frequently utilized in specialized fields such as medicine or industrial settings. Moreover, they often find it challenging to interpret mixed speech that blends general language with specialized jargon. This poses a challenge for automatic speech recognition systems operating within these specific domains.

arxiv-2406-18723.title: The local structure, electronic and optical properties of Pb(Mg 1/3 Nb 2/3 )O 3 -PbTiO 3 : first-principles study
arxiv-2406-18723.creator: M. Kovalenko, O. Bovgyra, V. Kapustianyk, O. Kozachenko
arxiv-2406-18723.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by M. Kovalenko, O. Bovgyra, V. Kapustianyk, O. Kozachenko. Pb(Mg 1/3 Nb 2/3 )O 3 -PbTiO 3 perovskite-based crystals attract considerable scientific interest due to their interesting properties and possible use in piezoelectricity and photovoltaics. To understand the local structure and fundamental properties of such materials, in this work, we focused on the study within the density functional theory of structural, electronic, and optical properties of Pb[(Mg 1/3 Nb 2/3 ) 0.75 Ti 0.25 ]O 3 .

arxiv-2411-03381.title: Young Researchers School 2024 Maynooth: Lectures on CFT, BCFT and DCFT
arxiv-2411-03381.creator: Christian Northe
arxiv-2411-03381.description: Abstract These notes were presented at the Young Researchers School (YRS) in Maynooth in April 2024 and provide an introduction to Conformal Field Theory CFT, Boundary Conformal Field Theory (BCFT) and Defect Conformal Field Theory (DCFT). This class is mostly self-contained and includes exercises with solutions.

arxiv-2503-17542.title: Reporting on pTP sublimation during evaporation deposition
arxiv-2503-17542.creator: E. Kemp
arxiv-2503-17542.description: Abstract Noble liquid detectors rely on wavelength shifter materials, such as p-terphenyl (pTP) and Tetraphenyl-butadiene (TPB), which are widely used in neutrino and dark matter experiments. Given their importance, a thorough understanding and characterization of these compounds are essential for optimizing experimental techniques and enhancing detector performance.

arxiv-2505-07871.title: Evaluating Financial Sentiment Analysis with Annotators’ Instruction Assisted Prompting: Enhancing Contextual Interpretation and Stock Prediction Accuracy Conference: 5th ACM International Conference on AI in Finance; Nov 14–16, 2024; Brooklyn, NY
arxiv-2505-07871.creator: A M Muntasir Rahman, Ajim Uddin, Guiling “Grace” Wang
arxiv-2505-07871.description: Abstract . Financial sentiment analysis (FSA) presents unique challenges to Large Language Models (LLMs) that surpass those in typical sentiment analysis due to the nuanced language used in financial contexts. The prowess of these models is often undermined by the inherent subjectivity of sentiment classifications in existing benchmark datasets like FiQA and Financial Phrasebank.

arxiv-2508-00989.title: Angular Coefficients from Interpretable Machine Learning with Symbolic Regression
arxiv-2508-00989.creator: Josh Bendavid, Daniel Conde, Manuel Morales-Alvarado, Veronica Sanz, and Maria Ubiali
arxiv-2508-00989.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Josh Bendavid, Daniel Conde, Manuel Morales-Alvarado, Veronica Sanz, and Maria Ubiali. We explore the use of symbolic regression to derive compact analytical expressions for angular observables relevant to electroweak boson production at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). Focusing on the angular coefficients that govern the decay distributions of W W and Z Z bosons, we investigate whether symbolic models can well approximate these quantities, typically computed via computationally costly numerical procedures, with high fidelity and interpretability.

arxiv-2509-24829.title: Continuous differentiability of the signum function and Newton’s method for bang-bang control
arxiv-2509-24829.creator: Daniel Wachsmuth, Gerd Wachsmuth
arxiv-2509-24829.description: Abstract We investigate bang-bang control problems and the possibility to apply Newton’s method to solve such kind of problems numerically. To this end, we show that the signum function is Fréchet differentiable between appropriate function spaces. Numerical experiments show the applicability of the resulting method.

arxiv-2510-08520.title: Tripartite entanglement in the HaPPY code is not holographic
arxiv-2510-08520.creator: Sriram Akella
arxiv-2510-08520.description: Abstract Holographic states satisfy several entropic inequalities owing to the Ryu-Takayangi formula. A drawback of these inequalities is that they only use bipartite entanglement in their formulation. We investigate a recently proposed “GHZ-forbidding” inequality, built out of the reflected entropy and the tripartite multi-entropy, that holds for holographic states.

pmc-10572326.title: Pasta Enriched with Carrot and Olive Leaf Flour Retains High Levels of Accessible Bioactives after In Vitro Digestion
pmc-10572326.creator: Veronica Conti, Chiara Piccini, Marco Romi, Patrizia Salusti, Giampiero Cai, Claudio Cantini, Wenhao Li

pmc-10608300.title: Chromatographic Analyses of Spirulina (Arthrospira platensis) and Mechanism of Its Protective Effects against Experimental Obesity and Hepatic Steatosis in Rats
pmc-10608300.creator: Fatma Arrari, Mohamed-Amine Jabri, Ala Ayari, Nouha Dakhli, Chayma Ben Fayala, Samir Boubaker, Hichem Sebai, Giovanni Tarantino
pmc-10608300.description: Background and Objectives: Obesity is currently a major health problem due to fatty acid accumulation and excess intake of energy, which leads to an increase in oxidative stress, particularly in the liver. The main goal of this study is to evaluate the protective effects of spirulina (SP) against cafeteria diet (CD)-induced obesity, oxidative stress, and lipotoxicity in rats.

pmc-11418139.title: Enhancing corrosion resistance of biodegradable magnesium with dicalcium phosphate dihydrate and Chlorella sp. biomass
pmc-11418139.creator: Lizeth del Carmen Gutierrez Pua, Lily Margareth Arrieta, Juan Carlos Rincon Montenegro, Leonardo Antonio Di Mare Pareja, Yaneth Pineda Triana, Ana Fonseca Reyes, Virginia Nathaly Paredes Mendez
pmc-11418139.description: SummaryMagnesium shows promise as a material for temporary fixation, yet its rapid corrosion poses health risks due to metal ion release. To mitigate these concerns, a biofunctionalization approach involving dicalcium phosphate dihydrate (DCPD) compounds and Chlorella sp. biomass was employed via electrodeposition, silanization, and dip-coating. Surface characterization using XRD, FTIR, and SEM confirmed successful deposition and immobilization.

pmc-11421078.title: Rate-Engineered Plasmon-Enhanced Fluorescence for Real-Time Microsecond Dynamics of Single Biomolecules
pmc-11421078.creator: Sjoerd
pmc-11421078.description: Single-molecule fluorescence has revealed a wealth of biochemical processes but does not give access to submillisecond dynamics involved in transient interactions and molecular dynamics. Here we overcome this bottleneck and demonstrate record-high photon count rates of >107 photons/s from single plasmon-enhanced fluorophores.

pmc-12432774.title: Identification of metabolic driver genes and targeted drug screening for lung adenocarcinoma metastasis at the single-cell resolution
pmc-12432774.creator: Liang Wu, Wenjuan Zhao, Xin Guo, Zuquan Hu, Sen Chen, Wenzhu Huang
pmc-12432774.description: BackgroundLung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the predominant type of lung cancer, and metastasis is a major cause of poor prognosis and death. Metabolic activation is a crucial factor driving tumor metastasis; however, the metabolic heterogeneity at the single-cell level presents significant challenges in targeting metabolism-related genes for treatment.

pmc-13286442.title: BUB1 in cancer genetics and oncogenomics: from chromosomal instability to therapeutic vulnerabilities
pmc-13286442.creator: Shuai Wang, Shizhen Liu, Yanan Zhou, Hongxiang Wang, Juxiang Chen
pmc-13286442.description: BUB1 is a serine/threonine kinase and a core component of the spindle assembly checkpoint that safeguards faithful chromosome segregation during mitosis. Accumulating studies have shown that BUB1 is aberrantly expressed across multiple malignancies and contributes to tumor progression through both canonical mitotic functions and noncanonical extramitotic activities.

pmc-13382742.title: Study of Light Gas Generation Behavior during the Thermal Chemistry Conversion Process of Cattle Manure
pmc-13382742.creator: Xue Zhao, Xiaohe Xiong, Yinan Zhang, Houzhang Tan, Renhui Ruan
pmc-13382742.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). To investigate the thermal chemistry conversion behavior of cattle manure as a biomass fuel, the effect of three reaction ambiences (N2, air, and CO2) and four temperatures (350, 550, 750, and 950 °C) was studied on a fixed-bed reactor. The tested final products were divided into three categories: nitrogen-containing species (NO, NO2, HCN, NH3), carbon-containing species (HCN, CH4, CO, CO2), and others (SO2, HCl). As the temperature increased, HCN and NO always increased, while NH3 and NO2 increased first and then decreased.

pmc-13397313.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026).
